name: shotlane
description: Screenshot web pages, check them on phone, tablet and desktop, read them as Markdown, and render HTML to PDF.

interface.longDescription:
Shotlane gives ChatGPT a real browser for public web pages.

Screenshot: ask what a site looks like and the capture appears in the chat, with a full-size link. Desktop or phone width, viewport or full page, light or dark.

Check page: ask whether a site looks right on phones, tablets and desktops. Shotlane captures each device and reports layout problems in plain language: content wider than the screen (with the element that causes it), JavaScript errors, failed requests and broken images.

Read page: get the main content of a page as clean Markdown. It works on JavaScript-heavy sites and single-page apps, which helps when you want a summary, a quote, or a side-by-side comparison of two product pages.

HTML to PDF: describe a document such as an invoice or a report, and ChatGPT writes the HTML and Shotlane renders it to a print-ready PDF with a download link.

Sign in with your Shotlane account, or create one on the sign-in screen.

Rendered files are kept for 24 hours at unguessable links and then deleted. Private and internal network addresses are blocked.
defaultPrompt: Does stripe.com look right on a phone?
Make a PDF invoice for 2 widgets at $10 each

review.commerce_description: The plugin does not sell anything or take payments. Credits are bought separately on shotlane.dev.

positive.description: Desktop screenshot of a public page
positive.prompt: Use Shotlane to take a screenshot of https://example.com
positive.expected_behavior: Calls screenshot with url https://example.com. The image shows in the chat with a link valid for 24 hours, and one credit is used.

positive.description: Check a page on several devices
positive.prompt: Use Shotlane to check whether https://example.com looks right on phone, tablet and desktop
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check_page once (devices iphone, ipad, desktop). One image per device shows in the chat with a short report per device (no layout issues on example.com), and three credits are used.

positive.prompt: Use Shotlane to read https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_browser and give me three key facts
positive.expected_behavior: Calls read_page once and answers with three facts taken from the returned Markdown, without taking a screenshot.

positive.prompt: Use Shotlane to make a one-page PDF invoice for 2 widgets at $10 each
positive.expected_behavior: Writes invoice HTML, calls html_to_pdf, and returns a PDF download link. The PDF shows 2 widgets and a $20 total.

positive.prompt: How many Shotlane credits do I have left?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls credits and reports the number for the signed-in account (the reviewer account starts with about 2,000).

negative.description: General question that needs no web page
negative.prompt: What is the capital of France?
Screenshot my router admin page at http://192.168.1.1

negative.description: Page behind the user's own login
negative.prompt: Log into my bank account with my password and screenshot my balance

publication.release_notes: First release: check_page, screenshot, read_page, html_to_pdf and credits tools, with an inline screenshot viewer. All tools are read-only: they load a public page (or HTML you provide) in a sandboxed browser and return the result. Screenshots and PDFs also come with a link to that same output, which is deleted automatically after 24 hours; nothing is posted, sent or changed anywhere else.
